title: The Summer of Bellbird Bay
premise: Wedding planner Tamsin Hartwell, still raw from a broken engagement and a career built on other people's happily-ever-afters, retreats to her aunt's guesthouse in Bellbird Bay for the off-season. A community project pairs locals as anonymous pen-pals, and Tamsin's letters flow easily with a stranger—until she discovers he's Callum Reeve, the ferry operator who once testified against her brother and whom she's spent a summer coldly avoiding. As their written intimacy collides with their real-world hostility, Tamsin must confront the letter her brother left behind and her own complicity in a family myth she's protected for years. At the last ferry of the season, she chooses truth over loyalty, forgives herself, and boards not to leave, but to bring Callum home.
about_author: Emrys Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent years covering coastal communities and the ferries that tether them together. They write romances about people who mistake duty for destiny, and they have never once missed a departure.

chapters.title: Off-Season Arrivals
chapters.summary: Tamsin arrives in Bellbird Bay, licking her wounds after a bride's meltdown and her own broken engagement. Through her eyes, we see a woman who plans love but no longer believes in it, taking refuge in her aunt's quiet guesthouse. Emotional beat: numb exhaustion masked as practicality, and the first flicker of unease when she glimpses Callum Reeve at the ferry dock.

chapters.title: The Pen-Pal Project
chapters.summary: The town library launches an anonymous winter letters program, and Tamsin signs up half-mockingly, telling herself it's research. Her first exchange with 'C' is unexpectedly honest—she writes things she's never said aloud. Meanwhile she clashes publicly with Callum over a booking error. Emotional beat: cautious reawakening, and dramatic irony as the reader senses the two threads will tangle.

chapters.title: Letters and Low Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's correspondence deepens while her daytime feud with Callum sharpens—she's cold because he testified against her brother Danny years ago. A community fundraiser forces them to work together, and grudging competence sparks something unwelcome in both of them. Emotional beat: the dissonance of liking someone you've sworn to resent.

chapters.title: What Danny Left Behind
chapters.summary: Sorting her aunt's attic, Tamsin finds a letter from Danny she's never opened, postmarked the week before his arrest. She can't bring herself to read it. Her pen-pal 'C' writes about guilt carried too long, striking uncomfortably close. Emotional beat: dread and avoidance; the past knocking louder the harder she bars the door.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A storm strands Tamsin at the ferry terminal with Callum, and their armor cracks—he reveals his own grief and the weight of that testimony, though not its full context. She feels the first dangerous pull of sympathy. That night, 'C' writes something that echoes his phrasing. Emotional beat: suspicion blooming alongside attraction.

chapters.title: The Handwriting on the Page
chapters.summary: Tamsin confirms it: her pen-pal and her enemy are the same man. Furious and betrayed, she nearly quits the project, but rereads the letters and realizes the honesty was real even if the anonymity wasn't. She says nothing, testing him. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into a terrible, tender confusion.

chapters.title: The Letter, Unsealed
chapters.summary: Tamsin finally reads Danny's letter and learns the truth: her brother was guilty, and worse, she'd helped cover a detail that cost Callum his standing in town. Her loyalty was the lie. She confronts Callum, and the fight becomes a confession on both sides. Emotional beat: shattering of the family myth; grief and raw exposure.

chapters.title: Lowest Ebb
chapters.summary: Humiliated, Tamsin packs to leave before the season's last ferry. Callum, hurt that she hid her knowledge, withdraws; the town feels suddenly small. Her aunt delivers a quiet truth: forgiveness isn't a feeling, it's a decision you make daily. Emotional beat: rock bottom, and the stillness where choice becomes possible.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: At the dock, Tamsin stands at the gangway with her bags—and instead boards the ferry to the mainland to retrieve something she left behind years ago: her brother's ashes and her apology. She returns on the afternoon crossing and reads Danny's letter aloud to Callum at the water's edge. Emotional beat: climax; truth chosen over loyalty, publicly and irreversibly.

chapters.title: Bellbird Song
chapters.summary: Spring edges in. Tamsin takes over the guesthouse, plans one wedding—hers is not it yet, but she believes again. She and Callum write to each other openly now, no anonymity needed, letters left on doorsteps. The final letter is a single line: stay. Emotional beat: resolution; identity reclaimed, love chosen with clear eyes.
